Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Global Insure Holdings Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Insure Holdings' Third Quarter earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer; Jennifer Morales, Chief Operating Officer; Thomas Hale, Chief Claims Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Global Insure Holdings' performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by robust share repurchase activity, elevated investment income yields, refined actuarial assumptions enhancing reserve precision, strategic pricing changes boosting premium volume, favorable combined ratio guidance, solid premium growth outlook, increased dividend payments, and declining customer acquisition cost trends. Our commitment to innovation and customer service continues to drive our success.

David Patel, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

David Patel: Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $2.15 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included strong operating cash flows, earned premium expansion, underwriting discipline, investment spread widening, capital returns to shareholders, and efficiency gains across sales and operations. Our combined ratio was 93.2%. Investment income for the quarter was $465 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with our consolidated RBC ratio at 562%. Our expense ratio also improved to 26.8%.

Let me expand on some of these highlights, starting with our investment income yield, which remains a standout contributor to our P&L in this evolving market. Our investment income yield, measured as annualized net investment income over average invested assets, stood at 4.15% for the quarter on our approximately $145 billion general account portfolio, up 45 basis points from the prior quarter and 85 basis points year-over-year from 3.30%. This drove the $465 million in net investment income, an 18% increase from last year, fueled by reinvestments at higher rates with the 10-year Treasury averaging 4.25%. Our forward book yield reached 4.45%, supported by extending portfolio duration to 5.8 years to match our 6.1-year liabilities while capturing term premiums. Spread income added 220 basis points, from our 28% allocation to investment-grade corporates, especially financials and utilities, where OAS tightened to 105 basis points.

The portfolio is conservatively positioned: 72% fixed income including 45% U.S. Treasuries and agencies, 22% IG corporates, and 5% in high-quality RMBS and CLOs yielding 6.2%; 12% equities focused on dividend aristocrats in the S&P Insurance Index at 2.8% yield; and 16% alternatives like core REITs and insurance-linked cat bonds at 7.1%. Credit quality is top-tier at 98% NAIC 1-rated, avoiding riskier office CRE or sub-BBB names. In the U.S., which is 65% of assets, we benefited from high-yield munis; Europe at 20% locked in UK gilts and Bunds at 3.8% with FX hedges; and Asia-Pacific at 15% shifted to SGD IG names. We've enhanced this with BlackRock's Aladdin for 20% better yield modeling, a $2 billion private credit pilot targeting 7-8% yields, and 25% ESG-compliant new buys. We anticipate Q4 yields at 4.1-4.3%, full-year 2024 at 4.0%, and resilience into 2025 even with Fed cuts, outperforming peers with shorter durations.

Shifting to underwriting metrics, our Q3 combined ratio of 93.2% exceeded expectations, thanks to CAT losses at just 1.8 points and 5.1% net rate gains in personal auto alongside 7.3% in workers' comp. Loss ratio was 66.4%, expense ratio 26.8%. For Q4 2024, we guide to 94-96%, midpoint 95%, with loss ratio 67-69% incorporating 3-4 points of CATs from winter storms and wildfires, ex-CAT attritional at 64-65% amid 6.2% auto inflation and 5.8% workers' comp medical trends, moderated large losses at 2.5 points via ML risk selection. Expense ratio 27-27.5% reflects marketing for telematics but offset by 87% STP rates. Full-year 2024 narrows to 94.5%, better than prior due to lower-than-planned $1.1 billion CATs and 4.8% rate gains, after non-renewing $450 million underperformers. For 2025, we target 93-95%, midpoint 94%, driven by GenAI underwriting triage cutting loss ratios 40-50 basis points, parametric reinsurance, U.S. at 94%, Europe 92% with cyber growth, Asia-Pacific 97% offset by Australian comp expansion. This leverages hardening reinsurance renewals and caps inflation risks.

Premium growth was another strength, with Q3 net written premiums up 8.2% to $4.7 billion year-to-date momentum at 7.5%. For Q4 2024, we expect 6-8% growth, full-year 7.5-8%, from 4-5% earned rates, 88-90% retention via AI models, U.S. at 7%, Europe 15%, Asia-Pacific 12%. For FY 2025, 9-11%, high-end of peers, with 70% organic from ZenithEdge 2.0 telematics and 5.5% renewals, 30% inorganic like $1.2 billion EuroRisk acquisition; personal lines 10-12%, commercial 8-10%, specialty 12-15%, life/health 7-9%. Risks balanced by 92-95% combined ratio target.

Our pricing discipline played a pivotal role here, delivering 9.2% net written premium growth to $14.8 billion despite inflation in auto repairs up 12%, medical at 7%, and secondary perils. Embedded rates hit 11.8%, boosting average premiums 10.5%, offset by 1.2% policy contraction. Personal lines auto up 7.8% to $5.2 billion on 12-15% hikes and telematics; homeowners 11.3% on 14.2% rates; commercial 12.4% to $4.6 billion on 10.5%; specialty/international 9.1%. U.S. Northeast auto thrived, California disciplined with non-renewals; Europe 11% property rates; Asia flat pending reinsurance. AI GLMs improved accuracy 15%, retention 87.2%, new business up 6%. Q4 rates 9-10%, sustaining 8%+ growth.

Capital management shines through our share repurchases, a key to enhancing value with shares undervalued versus embedded value. In Q3, we repurchased $525 million at $48.72 average, retiring 10.8 million shares or 1.2% of float, year-to-date $1.85 billion up 28% from 2023, averaging $617 million quarterly on $2.3 billion cash flows from 92.8% P&C ratio and higher yields. $5 billion authorization has $3.15 billion left, executed opportunistically via 10b5-1 plans, 65% below 0.85x $58.42 adjusted tangible book. U.S. 72% premiums funded most via $420 million P&C profits on 9.2% auto/7.5% comp rates; Europe $180 million excess moderated for IFRS 17/Basel IV; Asia lighter for health growth. Aligns with Capital First framework exceeding 9.2% cost of equity, accretive 2.5% to 2025 EPS per stochastic models with $4.2 billion cat XL. Q4 $800 million-$1 billion, potentially accelerating if rates >4%, ahead of peers on 115% cash conversion.

Dividends complement this, with Q3 $0.75 per share declared, full-year 2023 $2.90 up 8.5% at 44.8% payout on $6.42 operating EPS, 2.2x coverage from $2.1 billion free cash on $1.8 billion investment income at 4.8% yields. Decade CAGR 9.2% beating peers, book value up 12.3% to $78.50, ROE 14.8%. U.S. commercial 89.2% ratio, telematics 180 bps loss improvement; Europe life 14% growth; Asia 22%. AI claims at 95% digital, $300 million ILS, ESG green bonds sustain mid-single digit growth to $3.05-$3.15 in 2024 at 3.4% yield.

Actuarial refinements impacted results with $285 million pre-tax reserve strengthening, 8 bps to book value: $210 million P&C adverse from 5.1% loss trends in workers' comp/GL (medical +150 bps over CPI), 7.8% auto severity; offset by $75 million life releases on -2.5% mortality, MP-2023 longevity, 4.75% discount. U.S. 75% hit from litigated claims; Europe $30 million milder; Asia $15 million. ML stochastic reserving cut uncertainty 22%, IFRS 17 CSM -4%. Filed 9.5% comp rates, XOL caps tails; neutral H2 absent inflation spike.

Finally, customer acquisition costs declined to $287 per new customer, down 12% YoY from $326, 5% sequentially, beating $350-400 peer average for 1.2 million adds up 18%. Digital 45% at $142 CAC via AI targeting 4.5x ROAS; agents 30% $456 mitigated by portals; embedded 25% $189 via Uber/Lowe's. Auto $265, commercial $1,240. U.S. $278 down 13%, Europe $312 up 8%, Asia $210 down 25%. GenAI lead scoring targets 15-20% more cuts, 68 NPS, 92% renewals for 4x+ LTV/CAC.

These elements position us strongly.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial lines. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including advanced machine learning models for pricing accuracy and dynamic rate adjustments aligned with loss cost trends.

Robert Kline: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income and alternatives, maintaining high credit quality and liquidity.

Thomas Hale: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including AI-driven adjudication and digital straight-through processing. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times by 22% and improved claims resolution rates now at 95%.

Elena Vasquez: We are making significant investments in technology to enhance our operations and improve the customer experience. Our new cloud-based policy and claims platform integrated with partners like Guidewire is expected to drive significant efficiencies and cost savings, with early ROI from 87% automation.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the share repurchase activity and future deployment?

David Patel: Good morning, Alex. As I detailed, our Q3 $525 million buybacks at compelling valuations continue our opportunistic approach under the $5 billion authorization. With $3.15 billion remaining and strong cash flows, we plan $800 million to $1 billion in Q4, prioritizing if shares stay discounted to book value, balancing with growth while exceeding our cost of equity.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of persistent inflation on your business?

David Patel: Certainly, Jordan. Inflation in repairs, medical, and social costs remains a focus, but our 11.8% pricing, actuarial updates to 5.1% trends, and ML analytics have kept loss ratios controlled at 66.4% ex-adjustments. Reinsurance and non-renewals de-risk us, supporting 94.5% full-year combined ratio.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Gonzalez: What is the expected impact of potential regulatory changes around IFRS 17 and Solvency II on your underwriting strategy?

Lisa Chen: Thanks, Maria. We've proactively aligned with IFRS 17 CSM adjustments and Solvency II recals, moderating European activity but growing cyber and parametric lines. Our 210% SCR coverage and quota shares ensure resilience, targeting 92% Europe combined ratio in 2025.

Operator: Our next question comes from Kevin Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Kevin Patel: Can you elaborate on the expected benefits of the new technology platform?

Elena Vasquez: Absolutely, Kevin. The platform boosts STP to 87%, cuts cycle times 25%, and integrates telematics for 18% lower losses in UBI cohorts. Combined with GenAI triage, it shaves 40-50 bps off ratios and supports CAC declines, with $150 million FY24 capex yielding 2-3% EPS lift.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: On premium growth and combined ratio guidance, any sensitivities?

David Patel: Emily, our 9-11% 2025 premium guide assumes 5.5% rates and 89% retention, with 93-95% ratios resilient to $1 billion cats or recession via diversified books. Upside from AI pricing and acquisitions like EuroRisk.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] That covers our questions for now.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Global Insure Holdings. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
